title: PRD: Hosted API Interop Smoke Specs + Launch Runbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket defines a compact PRD and a smoke-test-driven launch runbook for the unified hosted inference surface (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). Goal is to provide a minimum set of behavioral and interoperability checks ("smoke specs") that validate cross-model compatibility, routing fallbacks, and telemetry signals prior to gated launch. The doc prioritizes operational safety, measurable acceptance criteria, and clear escalation/playbook steps for failures discovered during rollout.
background: Multiple recent launches surfaced edge cases where different model families (decoder-only vs. encoder-decoder) and payload modes (streaming vs. non-streaming) would behave inconsistently across the hosted surface. Engineering has implemented kernel-level fallbacks and an adaptive routing table, but we lack a concise set of canonical smoke tests that product, QA, and SRE can run during canary and regional launches. This PRD defines that canonical set plus an ops playbook for rollouts.
goals: Define a minimal, automatable smoke-spec suite covering chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank
Ensure deterministic behavior for critical tenants: routing fallback, streaming consistency, token accounting
Provide rollout gates and rollback criteria tied to telemetry (latency, error-rate, quality regressions)
Ship a single-page launch runbook engineers and SREs can follow during canary and GA
non_goals: Full test matrix for all model variants (out of scope; we'll reference broader test docket)
Long-term UX changes to SDKs (handled in separate SDK initiatives)
Performance micro-optimizations — this is validation and ops tooling only
in_scope: Smoke-spec definitions (inputs, expected outputs, tolerance thresholds)
Telemetry and dashboard definitions used as rollout gates
Launch runbook steps: canary, regional ramp, GA checklist
out_of_scope: Model training, fine-tuning, or eval authoring (only pre-existing evals referenced)
SDK surface changes and deprecation timelines
requirements: API contracts: requests and responses must adhere to current hosted API schema across all four endpoint types
Streaming parity: streaming chunks must arrive in order and contain the same aggregated tokens as non-streaming response for the same prompt
Token accounting: per-request token usage reported in telemetry within ±1% of billing computation
Fallback behavior: if primary model is unavailable, routed fallback model must provide same response shape and signal via header X-Redwood-Fallback: <model-id>
Quality thresholds: predefined prompt set must not regress more than 5% in BLEU/ROUGE/embedding cosine similarity depending on endpoint (see acceptance criteria)
Error classification: transient (5xx) vs permanent (4xx) must be logged, surfaced to Sentry, and included in canary dashboard
smoke_specs: Chat basic flow: 3-turn conversation, verify context preservation, streaming vs non-streaming equivalence, max latency 250ms p50 for short prompts
Completions edge-case: long prompt (3k tokens) to validate kv-cache continuity and correct end-of-sequence handling
Embeddings stability: 20 canonical inputs; average cosine similarity vs baseline embeddings >= 0.92
Rerank deterministic sample: given 10 documents and a query, top-3 order stability vs baseline >= 0.95
Fallback simulation: force primary model OOS and assert response includes X-Redwood-Fallback header and success rate >= 98%
Telemetry smoke: verify token_count, request_id, latency_ms, gateway_route, model_variant fields populate for each request
acceptance_criteria: All smoke_specs pass in canary region for 48 hours with no critical incidents
Canary latent error-rate (5xx) < 0.5% and no customer-impacting 4xx spikes
Telemetry signals available in the Console dashboard and mapped to alerting channels (PagerDuty/SLA)
telemetry_and_dashboards: Create canary dashboard: 1) Total requests, 2) 5xx/4xx rates, 3) p50/p95 latency by endpoint, 4) token accounting variance, 5) model fallback rate
Set alerts: 5xx > 1% for 10m —> P0 on-call, fallback rate > 2% sustained —> investigate routing config
Tagging: every smoke run must include tag smoke_run_id and environment:canary/region to filter telemetry
rollout_strategy: Step 0: Run PRD review and obtain engineering + SRE sign-off
Step 1: Deploy canary to single region (us-west-2), enable smoke-specs and dashboard. Duration: 48 hours
Step 2: Gradual regional ramp (eu-central-1, us-east-1) after 72h stable canary. Run smoke-specs for 24h in each region
Step 3: Monitor 7-day GA window with post-launch quality checks and automatic rollback policy if acceptance criteria violated
Rollback policy: revert model routing and tenant assignment if critical metrics breach thresholds for 15 continuous minutes
launch_runbook: Pre-launch: Confluence PRD link verified and signoffs collected from Eng, SRE, DevRel
Canary run: kick off automated smoke-spec suite via CI job smoke/canary/run with tag smoke_run_id
Canary monitoring: SRE to watch Dashboard A (Canary) and Slack channel #canary-alerts
Escalation: If 5xx > 1% for 10m, page on-call and pause rollout; collect traces and open ENG incident ticket
GA checklist: API docs updated, SDK compatibility tests green, cost telemetry validated, post-launch comms drafted
open_questions: Q1: Do we include sampling of long-running streaming sessions in smoke-specs? (Implied cost overhead)
Q2: Should rerank smoke-spec include humans-in-the-loop verification for quality or rely solely on metrics?
Q3: What exact tolerance threshold should be used for embedding drift beyond the canonical set?
decisions: D1 (2026-02-24): Keep smoke-spec set intentionally small (<=6 tests) to enable fast CI runs — agreed by Eng/PM/SRE
D2 (2026-03-01): Signal fallback via response header X-Redwood-Fallback; implement both header and telemetry metric fallback_rate — approved
D3 (2026-03-05): Use cosine threshold 0.92 for embeddings smoke-spec; product accepted potential false negatives for rare edge inputs

notes: This PRD is intentionally condensed to fit in a single Linear ticket; full test matrices and broader QA plans live in linked Confluence pages. The key differentiator is emphasizing 'smoke'—fast, automatable checks that reduce launch friction while catching high-impact regressions.
